findings.title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache ends by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) to touch SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object (validation error: data needs at least one field), and updateMany does not apply @updatedAt anyway, so {} cannot bump the column. unwatchCalendar in this file calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after deleting cache, and Google webhook/cron refresh uses the same method. Those flows now throw after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted, so a successful cache write is reported as a failure and retried. The new UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so this call does not serve the feature; remove it, or if the touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() } using UpdateManyMutationInput (the new repository method is typed as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which allows relation ops updateMany cannot apply).

findings.title: Delete cache leaves stale status in the UI
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper loads that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes onChanged through as an optional prop, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old cacheUpdatedAt and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the page keeps offering to delete it until a full remount.

findings.title: Cache status treats expired rows as live cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups CalendarCache by credentialId and returns max(updatedAt) with no expiresAt filter. Availability reads (getCachedAvailability) ignore rows whose expiresAt is in the past, but those rows are not deleted. Any leftover expired row still yields a cacheUpdatedAt, and CredentialActionsDropdown treats a truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache. Google connections whose cache has expired still show "Last updated" and "Delete cached data" even though that cache is not served.

findings.title: updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written
findings.body: The migration adds CalendarCache.updatedAt NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(). Every existing row, including stale or expired cache, receives the migration transaction time rather than when the cache value was actually written. The new UI displays that column as "Last updated", so after deploy every Google credential that has any CalendarCache row looks freshly synced until the next Prisma upsert. The leading comment is also wrong: it says the column is added without a default and cannot be applied to a non-empty table, but the SQL does add a default. Backfill from a real write time, or leave the column nullable so legacy rows show as unknown instead of a false timestamp.

findings.title: In-memory delegation calendars cannot see or delete cache
findings.body: Cache status is loaded only via connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId) and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. In-memory delegation credentials use negative credential IDs: calendar-cache.repository.ts treats credentialId < 0 as invalid for DB writes and reads those users' cache by userId plus key, not by the synthetic id. The status query therefore returns nothing for those connections, so the dropdown never shows cache. deleteCache.handler.ts (credential lookup where id = credentialId and userId = session user) also cannot find an in-memory delegation credential and throws "Credential not found or access denied". Org users on delegated Google Calendar cannot view or clear the cache this feature is meant to manage.

findings.title: Webhook helper writes the wrong .env and fails on Linux
findings.body: ENV_FILE is the relative path "../.env", resolved from the process cwd rather than the script directory. Running ./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root (the usual invocation) creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL where the app reads it; it can also modify an unrelated project's env file. The update on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS syntax; GNU sed on Linux errors and does not update the file. cleanup() then exits 0 even when URL extraction fails, so the failure is easy to miss.

findings.title: No tests for deleteCache ownership check
findings.body: deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes every CalendarCache row for a credential after a single findFirst on id plus userId, and the PR adds no tests. Nothing asserts that another user's credentialId is rejected, that a missing credential deletes zero rows, or that a negative in-memory delegation id is denied. That where clause is the only authorization control; a regression would wipe another user's calendar cache without the suite catching it.
